findings.text: Provides acquisition of a user range into caller storage with on demand faulting. Empty requests complete with zero. Start addresses are normalized for the target context before lookup. When output storage is supplied the service installs managed references and cache maintenance for each subpage, otherwise it only ensures presence. Success reports a page count and any partial progress is returned in preference to a later error.

Offers single address fault resolution for read or write intent with optional retry support. The region must permit the requested direction under VM_READ and VM_WRITE plus platform data access approval for remote cases. The generic fault handler outcome determines next steps, with completion and retry both reestablishing shared protection and reporting new ownership, while error outcomes map to errno failures.

Supplies range prepopulation for a single region and for arbitrary intervals. The single region form skips VM_LOCKONFAULT without work, rejects inaccessible protections, selects write faulting only for private writable regions, and otherwise uses forced touch with optional unlockable waiting. The interval form walks intersecting regions, skips device mapped types, aligns to region bounds, and either aborts or continues past failures depending on caller tolerance.

Provides byte granularity user access probes that return the not yet accessible tail length instead of failing directly. Page stepping probes advance one page at a time with overflow termination and use begin and end access windows around single byte accesses. The safe write probe resolves each page through the fault service under shared protection, and the subpage probe refines page level success with finer writability verification.

An alternate locked acquisition path without faulting validates each page then translates directly and takes a reference. It stops at the first missing region or unsuitable mapping and reports how many pages were translated, or a fault when none were translated. Forced access relaxes required rights to potential rights while normal access requires current rights.

Supports durable pin establishment by collecting and migrating unsuitable containers. The scan counts every folio that fails long term pinnability, leaves pinnable entries untouched, isolates ordinary entries after cache draining and huge entries through dedicated isolation, and accounts isolated pages. Migration targets any node with user allocation for long term pin purpose, converts coherent device pins to ordinary references before device migration and otherwise drops pins before moving the list, returning a retry request on success and restoring state on busy or memory failure.

Reference modes FOLL_GET and FOLL_PIN are mutually exclusive. Pin mode records that the address space contains pinned content and is never implied, while get mode is implied when output storage is present without pin mode. FOLL_TOUCH marks access, FOLL_FORCE broadens permission checks, and FOLL_DUMP combines forced get semantics for dump use. Population for fault in adds poison reporting with FOLL_HWPOISON and FOLL_MADV_POPULATE plus FOLL_UNLOCKABLE waiting and optional FOLL_WRITE direction.

Region suitability depends on direction and mapping type. Read intent needs VM_READ while write intent needs VM_WRITE unless FOLL_FORCE is present, in which case VM_MAYREAD and VM_MAYWRITE suffice. VM_IO and VM_PFNMAP mappings are excluded from population and from the simplified path. Special populate lookup distinguishes missing regions from flag mismatches with different errors, and inaccessible protections fail population.

Shared address space protection asserted by mmap_assert_locked is acquired killably by mmap_read_lock_killable when the caller arrives unlocked and otherwise by mmap_read_lock, and released by mmap_read_unlock. Retry capable operation may drop and reacquire that protection, tracked by a caller visible locked flag, and must release before return whenever this call acquired it or observed a drop. Completion and retry outcomes reacquire before reporting, and killable acquisition failure aborts with a retryable error.

Isolation of huge containers for migration is serialized by a global hugetlb lock held with interrupts disabled across validation and queueing. Membership and migratability plus an extra reference are checked under that lock, migratability is cleared before moving the entry to the caller list, and the lock is then released.

Durable pin handling uses a container named pages_or_folios with a shared union for members pages and folios viewed as entries, plus discriminant has_folios and length nr_entries. Retrieval yields the owning folio for an index regardless of mode, clearing nulls an entry after its reference is transferred, release drains all remaining entries according to the discriminant, and iteration skips all page entries covered by the current large folio extent before returning the next distinct folio.

Fault progress follows a retry protocol using FAULT_FLAG_ALLOW_RETRY and FAULT_FLAG_TRIED plus VM_FAULT_COMPLETED and VM_FAULT_RETRY and VM_FAULT_ERROR. When the handler reports completion or retry the resolver reacquires shared protection, marks ownership, and either returns or loops with tried set. The outer acquisition loop resumes at the faulting offset after a drop, reissues single page attempts with tried set, checks for pending signals before each retry, and continues until ownership stabilizes or the range completes.

Interval region lookup asserts shared protection and queries the ordered address space tree with an inclusive end derived from the exclusive bound. Both memory models share this contract. The main acquisition path also recognizes a special gate area when ordinary lookup fails and obtains its page through a dedicated gate service before continuing with normal multi page accounting.

Crash dump collection retrieves a single page with FOLL_FORCE and FOLL_DUMP and FOLL_GET under the locked acquisition service and converts any non unitary result to null. Callers provide the target address and a lock ownership cell that the service updates according to whether protection was acquired or dropped.

Several conditions abort acquisition without guaranteeing progress. A pending fatal signal always interrupts, and any pending signal interrupts when FOLL_INTERRUPTIBLE is requested. Poisoned contents, missing regions, unsuitable flags, and mappings that lack a backing structure each produce distinct failures, with EBUSY and EAGAIN treated as zero progress to terminate the current attempt. Zero total progress without FOLL_NOWAIT is escalated to a fault.

Range services operate at page granularity with page aligned bounds and page sized steps, coalescing contiguous pages of one large folio up to the remaining length. Empty ranges return zero, acquisitions return a page count, probes return remaining byte counts, dump returns either a page or null, device migration returns zero or busy, and long term migration setup returns a retry request. Failures use negative errno values including EFAULT and ENOMEM and EINTR and EBUSY and EAGAIN and EHWPOISON and EINVAL.
